# edgeslm


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

edgeslm fine-tunes small language models (SLMs) for narrow,
domain-specific tasks, and runs them on edge hardware such as a
Raspberry Pi 5 or an Arduino UNO Q. A large hosted model can do the same
tasks, but every call costs money and energy, data leaves the site, and
the service depends on a provider and a network. A narrow task that
repeats every day uses only a small part of a large model’s expertise,
so a small model trained for it can do the job locally.

The pipeline is domain-neutral: a task is defined by data, namely its
input format, its output format and its examples. It goes from synthetic
inputs and outputs written by a large teacher model, through LoRA
fine-tuning and evaluation, to a GGUF model that llama.cpp runs on the
board. The approach is described, and refined as the project goes, in
[Scope](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/design/scope.html).

## The first task

The first task comes from
[speaking-plants](https://fr.anckalbi.net/speaking-plants/), which
detects water stress in coffee plants with sensor nodes. Each day, code
in the domain project produces a *triage* for each farm: which nodes to
watch or fix, how severe each problem is, and what the data shows about
its cause, such as whether water still reaches the soil. The SLM turns
the triage into a short WhatsApp message for the farmer, with an action
for each problem.

The real triage does not exist yet, so
[`coffee`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/coffee.html)
generates synthetic records that follow the triage contract in the
scope, using the tuple sampler in
[`synth`](https://franckalbinet.github.io/edgeslm/synth.html). Here is
one record:

``` python
triage(dict(problem='water stress', pattern='cluster', severity='moderate'), random.Random(0))
```

    {'farm': 'Fazenda São João',
     'date': '2026-05-17',
     'nodes': 45,
     'items': [{'problem': 'water stress',
       'location': 'Block B, drip line B1',
       'pattern': 'cluster',
       'severity': 'moderate',
       'since': 'since Friday',
       'soil_water': 'arriving',
       'nodes_flagged': 6,
       'nodes_in_group': 7,
       'amount': 'almost all'}]}

A message for this record could read:

> ⚠️ Block B, drip line B1: almost all monitored plants have shown water
> stress since Friday, although their soil still gets water. Check the
> plants on this line for heat damage or root problems.

## Status

The project is building a proof of concept for the first task. The
scope, the synthetic triage records, the code checks, the teacher prompt
and the training data are done. Claude Haiku wrote the training
messages.

The [baseline](05_baseline.ipynb) and [fine-tuning](06_finetune.ipynb)
experiments compare Qwen3.5 0.8B and 2B on 270 test records. Untuned,
with rules and two examples in the prompt, they write messages that pass
every check for 123 and 70 records. Fine-tuned on 100 examples, with a
one-line prompt, both pass for 255 or more. The 0.8B fine-tuned on 199
examples passes for 264.

The fine-tuned 0.8B is [exported](07_export.ipynb) to GGUF for
llama.cpp. At 4 bits the file is 542 MB and still passes for 264 of the
270 records. The next step is to run it on an Arduino UNO Q and measure
speed, memory and quality on the board. [Running on the UNO
Q](07_export.ipynb#running-on-the-uno-q) gives the steps for the
colleague with the board.

## Install

Install the latest version from GitHub:

``` sh
pip install git+https://github.com/franckalbinet/edgeslm.git
```
